articles.title: Regulators approve another major investment package to stabilise grid tension
articles.excerpt: The new spending brings total commitments on this objective to well over a billion in the current cycle.
articles.author: carlos-cozar
articles.imageCaption: Transmission lines feeding into a substation | EP
content: Regulators have approved another major investment package aimed at stabilising tension across the national grid, extending a run of similar commitments made over the past year.
The new spending brings total commitments on this objective to well over a billion in the current cycle, according to figures reviewed by this outlet.

Some industry participants have raised questions about the pace of approvals relative to the underlying technical review, though the regulator maintains that each package was assessed on its own merits.

articles.title: The country's inflation gap with the rest of Europe widens for a second straight quarter
articles.excerpt: Economists point to energy costs and transport as the two categories driving most of the divergence.
articles.author: ruben-sampedro
articles.imageCaption: A fuel pump display showing current prices | EP
content: The inflation gap between the country and the rest of the eurozone widened for a second straight quarter, according to figures released this week.
Economists point to energy costs and transport as the two categories driving most of the divergence, with food prices contributing a smaller but still meaningful share.
The figures complicate the outlook for competitiveness heading into next year, several analysts said, though most expect the gap to narrow gradually as base effects fade.

articles.title: Employers increasingly turn to seven-day contracts as a route back to hiring
articles.excerpt: Roughly one in five contracts signed this year fall into this short-duration category, the next most common being one to three months.
articles.author: ruben-sampedro
articles.imageCaption: A hiring notice posted outside a storefront | EP
content: Employers are increasingly turning to seven-day contracts as a route back to hiring, according to labour ministry figures published this week.
Roughly one in five contracts signed this year fall into this short-duration category, with the next most common band running from one to three months.
Labour groups have called for a review of the trend, arguing it reflects continued caution among employers rather than a genuine recovery in permanent hiring.

articles.title: Banks raise deposit rates for the fourth time since the war, but still pay less than 2% in Europe
articles.excerpt: Two major lenders now offer 2.25% interest to selected customers, but this is not enough to keep up with European competitors.
articles.author: ruben-sampedro
articles.imageCaption: Coins stacked on a bank statement | EP
content: Two of the country's largest lenders raised deposit rates this week for the fourth time since the start of the conflict, offering 2.25% interest to selected customers.
The increase is still well short of what several European competitors are offering, prompting some savers to look abroad or into money market products instead.
Analysts expect further gradual increases as competition for deposits intensifies heading into next year.

articles.title: A major lender forecasts a 10% jump in housing prices this year on the way to 18% by 2028
articles.excerpt: The bank's most likely scenario points to a sharper rise than the 5.7% it projected six months ago.
articles.author: ruben-sampedro
articles.imageCaption: Construction cranes above a residential development | EP
content: A major lender has sharply raised its housing price forecast for this year, now projecting a 10% increase compared with the 5.7% it estimated six months ago.
Under its most likely scenario, the bank expects cumulative price growth of around 18% by 2028, driven by constrained supply in the largest cities.
The revised outlook adds to concerns about affordability for first-time buyers in urban areas already facing tight rental markets.
